title: Go SDK: Response Contracts, Typed Stream Inspector, and Generics Decode Patterns
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Ship a robust, ergonomically typed decoding surface for the Go SDK that covers both single-response and streaming responses. Deliver a small set of generics-based helpers (Decoder[T], StreamInspector, EnvelopeValidator) that make structured output decoding, retry-safe streaming, and batched stream merging straightforward for application engineers.

Background: Current Go helpers in the repo are untyped or ad-hoc for specific response shapes. As customers adopt structured outputs (JSON objects, arrays, and typed envelopes) we need a composable API that: (1) preserves low allocation/low-latency streaming paths, (2) surfaces decoding errors with clear locations for observability, and (3) integrates with the SDK retry semantics so partial streams do not produce duplicate side effects.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Decoder[T]: a generic helper that can decode a complete response (non-streaming) into typed structs using json.Decoder under the hood but with additional path-aware error messages.
- StreamInspector: a thin streaming combinator that accepts the raw token stream (chunks) and emits assembly events for typed decoders to consume; supports token boundaries across chunk splits, backpressure signaling, and idempotency markers to coordinate retries.
- EnvelopeValidator: small validator that enforces top-level contract (status, error, body) and maps to domain errors for the SDK.
- Examples: three cookbook examples (structured chat response, embeddings batch ingest, and streaming table rows) to live under examples/go/typed-output.
- Migration plan: compatibility layer that keeps existing Unmarshal helpers and exposes adapters to the new generics helpers.

Non-goals: full schema registry integration (deferred), adding reflection-based validation rules (deferred to follow-up), and changing wire protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Decoder[T] type compiles and passes unit tests for at least 3 domain shapes (ChatMessage, EmbeddingVector, TableRow)
StreamInspector correctly reassembles JSON tokens split across chunks in fuzz tests (>= 10k randomized cases)

Retry integration: when a streaming request is retried due to transient network failure, handlers using Decoder[T]/StreamInspector do not emit duplicate application-level 'commit' callbacks in the example harness
Docs: examples/go/typed-output contains 3 runnable examples and a migration guide from Unmarshal helpers
Benchmarks: end-to-end mean p95 token latency overhead < 5% relative to current untyped streaming path on our internal benchmark harness
comments: 2026-03-01 Ava Chen: Initial write-up and RFC sketched. Decided to prefer explicit token assembly over naive rebuffering to avoid O(n^2) copies for large streams.

2026-03-03 Luca Martinez: Spike completed; implemented prototype StreamInspector that uses a small ring buffer and emits 'partial token' / 'token complete' events. Observed a small allocation increase (~8%) but simplified error attribution significantly.

2026-03-05 Design review (Maya Patel): Recommend exposing two orthogonal APIs: Decoder[T].Decode(bytes) for sync flows and Decoder[T].BindStream(StreamInspector) for streaming. Also suggested adding a concise error type with byte offset + token path.
2026-03-07 Security review (Samir Gupta): Confirmed no new secret surfaces. If we add schema registry integration in future, require additional threat modeling.

2026-03-09 Performance notes (Luca Martinez): Microbenchmarks show p50 decode ~1.03x current path; p95 ~1.06x. Plan to add an opt-in zero-copy mode using github.com/valyala/fastjson in a follow-up if needed.
2026-03-10 QA (Nora Li): Fuzz harness running 24h found a token-splitting edge case when a UTF-8 rune boundary crosses chunk; added unit to fix reassembly logic.
notes: Trade-offs: chose explicit token assembly to keep semantics simple and error messages precise; this costs modest extra allocations. We will evaluate a zero-copy optimized path only if benchmarks show customer-visible regressions. API ergonomics prioritized for common patterns: single-object outputs and line-delimited JSON streams.
implementation_plan: 1) Merge prototype StreamInspector PR behind feature flag (timeline: 1 week). 2) Add Decoder[T] and EnvelopeValidator with unit tests (2 weeks). 3) Add fuzz tests and run 48-hour harness (1 week). 4) Add examples and docs, and schedule canary SDK release for beta customers (1 week).
migration_plan: Provide adapter: func FromLegacy(untyped func(io.Reader) (interface{}, error)) Decoder[interface{}] that wraps existing helpers. Notify customers via changelog; label new APIs beta and gated behind feature flag for one minor release.
